prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures an upward-tilted indoor counter scene where the overhead slatted ceiling (1.5 to 2.5 metres above) and left wall (2 to 3 metres to the left) appear brightest and nearest, while the recessed service counter alcove ahead sits further back at roughly 3.5 to 5 metres and the open doorway on the lower left recedes into pitch-black depth beyond 5 metres. Within the distant counter alcove, a box-like machine on the left stands slightly nearer (about 3.5 metres) in front of the recessed back wall and three menu boards, with nothing within arm's reach of the camera wearer and the lower counter mostly cut off by the bottom frame edge. Across the five frames, the spatial layout remains nearly static with only a slight camera shift that causes the foreground dispenser silhouette at the lower edge to sink further out of view after frame 2. Compared to RGB, the depth map clearly resolves the 3D relief of the individual ceiling beams, the step-back geometry of the wall alcove, and the deep passage through the left doorway despite heavy lighting glare. However, the map becomes unreliable across the lower counter in frames 3 to 5, where backlit menu glare and dark foreground shadows flatten the counter equipment and obscure a person's head barely visible at the bottom edge in RGB.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map is completely blank in frames 1 and 5, and in frames 2, 3, and 4 it detects only a single large light-blue mask labeled 'tv' spanning the lower-right counter alcove roughly 3.5 to 5 metres ahead of the camera wearer. This coarse mask sits below the unsegmented ceiling and to the right of the unsegmented left wall and doorway (2 to 4 metres away), extending down to the bottom image boundary where the lower counter is occluded by the frame edge. Nothing is detected within arm's reach of the camera wearer, and across frames 2 to 4 the upper edge of the 'tv' mask shifts slightly downward as the camera tilts subtly. While the mask roughly localizes the illuminated display niche in the middle frames, it offers less detail than RGB and is highly unreliable: it merges three distinct hanging menu boards, the surrounding recessed wall, and foreground counter equipment into a single blocky 'tv' region, misses the displays entirely in frames 1 and 5, and fails to segment the partially visible person at the bottom edge.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black across all five frames, detecting no yellow body skeletons or magenta hand skeletons anywhere in the scene. In the RGB strip, the camera is angled sharply upward toward the ceiling (1.5 to 2.5 metres above) and the upper wall of a counter 3.5 to 5 metres ahead, leaving no people or hands within arm's reach of the camera wearer. Although the top of a person's head is faintly visible at the bottom edge of the RGB frames in front of the menu boards (roughly 3.5 to 4 metres away and heavily occluded by the lower frame boundary), too little of their body is in view to determine their full posture or trigger a skeleton detection. Across all five frames, this complete absence of tracked keypoints remains unchanged as the camera makes only minor rotational adjustments. Consequently, the pose map provides no spatial information beyond confirming the absence of clearly visible full bodies or foreground hands, and is unreliable for detecting heavily cropped distant occupants at the edge of the field of view.
